notes: Two environment variables are required at run time and nothing secret is baked into the image: NORTHSTAR_ACCESS_TOKEN for the Northstar business APIs and CELECO_MODEL_GATEWAY_KEY for the Celeco model gateway. They are distinct credentials and not interchangeable. Copy .env.example to .env, fill both in, then: docker build -t northstar-triage . && docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 --env-file .env northstar-triage. Note that Docker's --env-file only parses KEY=value lines and silently ignores Key: value, so convert the supplied credentials file if it uses colons; GET /health reports whether each credential was actually loaded, never its value. The loader also accepts API_Access_Key and Model_Access_key as alternative names. Two optional settings bound how long a case waits on Northstar, with working defaults: NORTHSTAR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (5) and EVIDENCE_BUDGET_SECONDS (15). Results: 210 offline tests (no network, no model calls), 8/8 on the provided visible runner, 12/12 on scripts/demo.py. One model call per case. Model budget used: about 115 of 300. Two AI sessions, both exported in full under agent-sessions/ and indexed in AI_WORKLOG.md: a builder session and an independent black-box tester session whose 50-case suite is in tests/stress/. Credentials and my personal email are redacted from the transcripts with visible markers; deliberately invalid test keys are left intact. See SOLUTION.md for design decisions and QUALITY.md for the testing history and known limits.
